title: Erdős Problem #840: Quasi-Sidon Subsets

problemStatement.formal: \exists c, 2/\sqrt{3} \le c \le c_P \land \forall N, f(N) \sim c\sqrt{N}
problemStatement.plain: How does f(N) — the maximum size of a quasi-Sidon subset of {1,...,N} — grow asymptotically? Known bounds: (2/√3)√N ≤ f(N) ≤ 1.863√N. What is the exact constant?
whyMatters: Central open problem in additive combinatorics connecting Sidon sets, sumsets, and extremal graph theory
Resolution would settle whether the Erdős-Freud reflection construction is asymptotically optimal

open: Exact asymptotic constant c in [2/√3, c_P] ≈ [1.155, 1.863]
Whether the Erdős-Freud construction is optimal

currentState.focus: Axiomatized all known research bounds; file has 9 axioms, 0 sorries.
currentState.nextAction: Problem is open — full proof requires resolving the open conjecture.

knowledge.progressSummary: AXIOMATIZED: All 7 sorry-theorems + 2 broken proofs converted to axioms (9 total). 3 theorems have full proofs. File compiles cleanly.
insights: The Erdős-Freud lower bound construction B ∪ {N-b : b ∈ B} achieves 2/√3 ≈ 1.155 using a Sidon set B ⊆ [1,N/3]
Pikhurko (2006) improved the upper bound to ≈1.863 via connection to edge-magic graph labelings
The difference-set analog (A-A) has constant exactly 1 (Cilleruelo), showing sum version is structurally harder
Sidon sets have |A+A| = k(k+1)/2 exactly; quasi-Sidon requires only (1+o(1))·C(k,2)
The gap [1.155, 1.863] has been open since 1991 — this problem likely requires genuinely new techniques
